clauses.reason: The order approves the modifications of the Code of Fair Competition for the Textile Bag Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act: the operative words of the President's order are "do order that said modifications of the Code of Fair Competition for the Textile Bag Industry be, and they hereby are approved and made a part of said Code". The modifications operate only as a part of the code that the President approved on September 18, 1933 (held as EO 6293), so this approval had no effect apart from that code. An approved code had legal effect only through section 3 (under 3(b) its provisions became the standards of fair competition, under 3(c) the district courts could enjoin violations, under 3(f) violations were misdemeanors). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The approval therefore ceased to have operative effect on June 14, 1935. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended earlier, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

research_rationale:
EO 6529 was read in full in the registered APP transcription (common-crawl capture 2025-11-11T00:18:16Z). Identity: the census register row, the WPA 1944 numbered list (1933 Dec 23, p. 559, 'Modifications of Code of Fair Competition for the Textile Bag Industry approved') and the APP page record with the same sha256 agree on number, date and subject; the page heading names the order's number, its date matches, and the page record's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The order approves modifications of the Textile Bag Industry code on an application of the Textile Bag Industry Control Committee dated November 13, 1933, under Article VIII, Section (b) of the code (approved September 18, 1933), after the Administrator's report of December 14, 1933. It has one operative paragraph: adopting the report and findings and approving the modifications as 'a part of said Code'. Under the shared reviewed analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md, ADJUDICATION.json) a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935, when section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed the power to approve or prescribe codes and the provisions enforcing them; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded only as a validity characterization. Original not yet held; the working text is a labeled transcription under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling.

Recorded as a validity characterization of every section 3 approval (void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing), not as an end of this order's command; no held record shows that the government cancelled or suspended this code on May 27, 1935.
